default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-658.title: Classic pivot R/S rejection
E-658.hypothesis: Floor-trader pivot levels (R1/S1, R2/S2) from the previous session are watched by many desks; a poke through one that closes back inside means resting orders absorbed the push, so fade it.

E-659.title: Round-number rejection
E-659.hypothesis: Index round numbers (every 500/1000 points) hold clustered limit orders and option-strike hedging; a bar that reaches the next round level and closes back below it (or mirror) is rejected supply/demand.

E-660.title: Previous clock-block range break
E-660.hypothesis: The range of the previous 15/30/60-minute clock block is a reference for desks that schedule by the clock; a close beyond it in the next block shows that block's balance being rejected; follow.

E-661.title: Hour-turn continuation
E-661.hypothesis: Funds and execution algos rebalance at the top of the hour; when the move into the hour is larger than usual, the first bar of the new hour keeps the direction of that flow; follow.

E-662.title: Same-minute seasonal drift
E-662.hypothesis: If over the last 20 sessions the next 30 minutes from this clock minute drifted one way on average and in the median, recurring scheduled flow (opens, data, rebalancing) may repeat; trade that drift.

E-663.title: Weak-volume new extreme fade
E-663.hypothesis: A new window high/low printed on below-normal volume for the minute lacks participation; it is a liquidity poke, not acceptance, and tends to revert.

E-664.title: Previous-range exhaustion reversal
E-664.hypothesis: When the day has already travelled a set fraction of yesterday's whole range from the open, the typical daily range budget is spent; a bar closing against the move starts the give-back.

E-665.title: VWAP deviation z-score fade
E-665.hypothesis: Distance from VWAP scaled by its own session dispersion marks statistically stretched prices; market-order chasers overshoot and liquidity providers pull price back toward the day's fair value.

E-666.title: Previous-day midpoint reclaim
E-666.hypothesis: The midpoint of yesterday's range is the balance point of the previous auction; after dwelling on one side, a close across it means the market re-accepts the other half; follow.

E-667.title: Block close-location persistence
E-667.hypothesis: A clock block that closes in the top (bottom) slice of its range leaves one side unfilled; when the next block opens with a bar in the same direction, the unfilled orders continue the move; follow.
